title: Who Is Indigenous? The Politics of Tribal Identity Terminology in India and Bangladesh
gist: West Bengal's new BJP government, in power since May 2026, cancelled International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples events on August 9 without explanation, prompting protests from adivasi groups and opposition parties, who link it to the BJP's ideological rejection of adivasi identity; the piece examines tribal identity terminology politics in India and Bangladesh.

insights.claim: The BJP government that took power in West Bengal in May 2026 cancelled the state's International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples celebrations via an August 5 notice, after four days of statewide events the previous year.
insights.speaker: Snigdhendu Bhattacharya
entities: International Day of the World’s Indigenous Peoples
insights.so_what: Signals a new BJP state government reshaping identity policy in a formerly opposition-held state, a source of social friction.
insights.quote: The new Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government that came to power in May issued a notice on August 5, stating that this year’s celebration was cancelled.

insights.claim: Opposition figures such as CPI(M) leader Mayukh Biswas allege the cancellation stems from the BJP's ideological project of denying the adivasi identity of the tribal population.
insights.speaker: Snigdhendu Bhattacharya
insights.so_what: Contested tribal identity can affect land rights and resource projects in tribal areas.
insights.quote: “This is an assault on the indigenous people’s identity and pride,”
